I farm the full 10.1 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, so I will put all 10.1 mu into winter wheat first and then all 10.1 mu back into summer maize after wheat harvest. I am 61 and my household is small, so I will keep the system steady and practical rather than chase risk. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on stable water at the key stages instead of gambling on rainfall. For wheat, I will use improved seed, do rotary tillage, and put in moderate fertilizer with enough nitrogen to support tillering and grain filling, plus phosphorus for roots and some potassium for lodging resistance. I will irrigate a few key times and spray only as needed for weeds and common diseases. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is the most dependable way for me to hold yield on this land. I will keep fertilizer a bit stronger on nitrogen for maize, use lighter phosphorus and potassium than wheat, and irrigate at the critical stages if rain is short. I will stay with rotary tillage because it matches my labor, machinery habits, and the wheat-maize rotation well. My goal is not the highest possible yield, but a stable yield with costs and labor I can still manage well.
